name: Dr. Jayy
about: [color=#ed4990][size=2][font=-apple-system, system-ui, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif]Dr. Jayy Suzumiya, formerly Dr. Jane Suzumiya, is Director of Aomo Private Hospital, holding dual degrees in Medicine and Psychiatry.[/font][/size][/color]
lore:
[color=#1f1f1f][font="Google Sans Text", sans-serif]Her birth name was Jane. The name was given by her uncle, because after her parents passed away, she was raised by her maternal uncle and aunt. Her uncle was the Minister of Health, which meant Jane had no say in her own future; she was systematically forced into becoming a doctor and heavily pressured to assist in complex medical and scientific research. For someone so young, the burden was immense. She was even handed a high-ranking director position that left her physically and mentally exhausted. What Jane truly craved was the freedom to conduct her own independent research without being micromanaged or told what to do.

Perhaps that was why she secretly fell in love with skydiving-up in the open air, away from the suffocating expectations of her family, it made her feel as free as a bird. Ironically, before discovering that liberating feeling, she was actually terrified of heights. She was once invited to go skydiving, she trained and prepared thoroughly, but the moment the plane door opened, she fainted on the spot. That was until an unexpected assignment took her far beyond anything she had ever prepared for.

One day, Jane went to gather resources in a remote area on Planet Hazuniverse. She was accompanied by a pilot, Captain Navy. The atmosphere there was as safe as Earth's. In the middle of their journey, while they were having lunch, Captain Navy suddenly showed a severe allergic reaction. Jane panicked, because their food had been prepared nut-free. She immediately looked for an EpiPen in the first-aid kit, but it was empty. All of her medical equipment was empty! At the same time, the aircraft's engine malfunctioned. And worst of all, there was only one parachute left. Like it or not, they had to abandon the plane. Maybe because of the adrenaline rush, Jane managed to carry Captain Navy and jump. She swiftly deployed the parachute. For the first time, she wasn't afraid. She felt free, as if she had become one with the sky. They landed on a giant, soft flower. The flower had a sleeping effect, and they both fell asleep.

When they woke up, they were already surrounded by Hazuvians, the alien inhabitants of Hazuniverse. They were interrogated. Jane convinced them that they meant no harm and introduced herself as a doctor who was searching for medicine. That's when Jane learned that the remote village was struck by a strange pandemic. The villagers couldn't sleep, suffered from severe hallucinations, and some even died. That's why they isolated themselves, believing outsiders brought bad luck. Jane offered to help, but asked them to heal Captain Navy first. After Captain Navy recovered, Jane remembered the giant flower where they had landed. She did a quick research on the flower and successfully created a cure for the villagers. Thanks to her service, the village no longer isolated itself. As a token of gratitude, the villagers started calling her "Jayy" because they thought it was a cool name. The village chief also promised to help Jayy whenever she needed it in the future.

After the village matters were settled and they finally got a signal, Jane didn't immediately decide to return to Earth. Suspicious, she tried to search for news about Earth from Hazuniverse. And she was right. She found news about their disappearance. They had been missing for 6 months and had even been declared dead. Debris from the plane and her old ID were already at the Earth police station. Jane immediately showed the news to Captain Navy and convinced him that their deaths had been planned. They decided not to go home right away, but to gather and secure all the evidence from afar first.

Once they had enough evidence, they quietly returned to Earth using a warp-technology spaceship, heading straight to the police station to testify. The culprit was her own cousin, her uncle's daughter. She was the one who emptied the EpiPen, sabotaged the aircraft engine, and left only one parachute. She couldn't stand seeing Jane become a more brilliant and more celebrated doctor than herself.

A few weeks after that, she decided to go skydiving again. When the plane door opened, her friend turned to her and asked, "Are you ready now, Jane?"

She smiled, looking out into the open sky. "I'm not using that name anymore. Call me Jayy."

"Got it, Jayy," her friend grinned. "So, what's next for you after today?"

"Well, Packing up my things and moving out of my uncle and aunt's house," Jayy said, feeling a weight lift off her shoulders. "Beyond that... I don't know yet. We'll see."

With a nod of quiet confidence, she stepped to the edge and jumped into the sky-diving straight into her new life of complete freedom.[/font][/color]
